text:
Phillip Danault is back in Montreal, the team where he made his name as a shutdown center, and The Hockey Writers used the moment to revisit the trades that moved him around. So far the return looks better than last season did: Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in 2025-26.

He has 9 points in 23 games at 17.2 minutes, a scoring rate of 1.36 per 60 that is already well above last season's 0.87. The Canadiens control play with him on: 54.7% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances), 5 points better than without him. He kills penalties and does not shoot much.

Part of the scoring help has been luck around him. Montreal has scored 8.0 more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, which tends to fade. His own shooting, 8.6%, is on the low side of our range, so it is not his finishing doing the work. Our range for his season is 23 to 38 points. What we'd watch is whether the 5v5 chance share holds once the bounces even out.
